html:
Grégoire Kayibanda was the first president of Rwanda, from independence in 1962 until he was overthrown in 1973.

A Catholic journalist and teacher, he co-wrote the Hutu Manifesto of 1957, which called for an end to Tutsi rule, and founded the Parmehutu party, which led the Rwandan Revolution. As president he ran a one-party state that favoured Hutu from his home region of Gitarama.

When Tutsi exiles raided from abroad in 1963, his government answered with massacres of Tutsi at home. In 1973 Juvénal Habyarimana, an officer from the north, took power in a coup, and Kayibanda died in custody. His idea of Rwanda as a Hutu nation outlived him and was taken up by the planners of the genocide.
sum: Grégoire Kayibanda was the first president of Rwanda, from independence in 1962 until he was overthrown in 1973.
